chunks: And ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say:

There is no servant except that an angel is appointed over him, turning his neck so that he looks at his excrement. Then the angel says to him: O son of Adam, this is your provision, so look from where you took it and to what it has become.
So it is fitting for the servant at that moment to say: O Allah, provide me with the halal and keep me away from the haram.

key_terms.الْحَرَامَ: that which is unlawful and forbidden
key_terms.الْحَلَالَ: that which is lawful and permissible
key_terms.مَلَكٌ: an angel appointed over a person

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be said when reflecting on food, provision, and avoiding haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام teaches reflection on the origin and end of worldly provision, reminding the believer of the fleeting nature of what is consumed. It encourages moral awareness regarding halal and haram earnings and teaches a brief du'a asking Allah to grant lawful sustenance and distance one from the unlawful.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.38 - Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) used to say:
"There is no servant (of Allah (swt)) except that there is an angel appointed to turn his head to look at his excrement, and then the angel says to him:
'O’ child of Adam, this is your provision, so consider from where you took it and to what it has turned.'
It is appropriate for the servant at that moment to say:
Allāhumma urzuqnī al-ḥalāla wa jannibnī al-ḥarāma
‘O’ Allah (swt), grant me lawful provision and keep me away from the unlawful.'"
